headline: Germany's First Certified International Dark Sky Park
reservation: Entry to the island generally requires ferry transport; check current sailing schedules and municipal visitor requirements. There are no specific permits required for sky observation, though visitors should confirm local accommodation availability in advance as this is a protected nature area.

days.title: North Sea Astronomy
days.start: Suggested: 8 PM from the island center

stops.name: Spiekeroog
stops.detail: Experience one of Germany's first officially certified 'sky islands' recognized by the IDA for its exceptional starry skies. The lack of artificial light pollution makes this an ideal location for astronomy fans and nighttime nature observation.

days.driving: Allow for local walking; conditions vary based on tides and ferry times.
days.note: Pace your visit to allow for astronomical twilight, as the dark sky certification is the primary feature of this location.

intel.title: Ferry Transport
intel.text: Access to the island is via ferry from the mainland coast. Visitors should check the current tide-dependent schedules as crossing times change daily.

intel.title: Night Sky Observation
intel.text: Observation quality is highest during new moon phases. Official IDA certification ensures the island maintains low light pollution for optimal viewing.

intel.title: Energy and Supplies
intel.text: Specific fuel and supply availability on the island is not detailed in current dark sky records. Confirm logistics at the mainland ferry terminal before departure.

intel.title: Communication Coverage
intel.text: Evidence does not detail mobile signal strength for the island interior. Prepare for potential connectivity gaps in remote observation areas.

intel.title: Mainland Staging
intel.text: Parking is typically required at the mainland ferry port rather than on the island itself. Check local port authority signage for long-term parking restrictions.

plan.arrival: Arrive at the mainland ferry terminal to transfer to the island. Check into local accommodation before sunset to prepare for nighttime observation.
plan.vehicle: The island is car-free; visitors rely on walking or local transfers once they arrive by ferry.
plan.goldenHour: Dusk at the coast offers a transition into the certified dark sky environment, though specific viewpoint names are not provided.
